meta.title: Baseline — Brain health over time
meta.description: Short everyday activities that build your personal brain-health baseline and notice meaningful change early.

common.simulatedHint: This data is synthetic, for demonstration only.
common.screeningNotice: Baseline is a screening and monitoring tool. It does not diagnose any condition.

home.tagline: Know your usual. Notice change early.
home.intro: A few minutes of everyday activities, like remembering a shopping list or sorting medicines, build a picture of what is normal for you. Baseline then looks for meaningful change over time.

steps.title: Set your baseline
steps.body: Short activities for one week show what is usual for you.

steps.title: Check in briefly
steps.body: A few minutes a day, plus how you slept and how you feel.

steps.title: Get clear next steps
steps.body: Healthy habits, a repeat check, or a summary for your doctor when it helps.

dashboard.baselineBody: {done} of {total} short sessions done. Up to two a day works best.
dashboard.resetConfirm: This deletes everything stored on this device. Continue?

lab.title: Validation Lab
lab.intro: How well does Baseline separate real change from normal ups and downs, and is it equally good for everyone? We tested the full pipeline on a simulated cohort before any real use.
lab.label: Simulated: operating characteristics under stated assumptions. Not clinical accuracy.
lab.fastMode: Development run with a small cohort. Not reportable.
lab.missing: No results yet. Run: python -m baseline_lab.run
lab.setup: {users} simulated people · 2 years each · seed {seed} · protocol v{protocol} ({amendments})
lab.explorerBody: Move the Watch threshold. Stricter thresholds mean fewer false referrals but later or missed detection.
lab.lead: Median days from change onset to referral
lab.fairnessBody: Same threshold for everyone. Gaps beyond the limits are shown honestly.
lab.difBody: We planted 3 unfair items per task family. Did the check find them, and did it wrongly flag fair items?
lab.pathwayBody: Model comparison using the Al Ain diagnosis-delay study. Not observed outcomes.
lab.sensitivityTitle: What if our assumptions are wrong?
lab.timelapseTitle: Three simulated people over two years
lab.pilotBody: These numbers come from a model. Before any real use, a local pilot with Arabic- and English-speaking older adults in Abu Dhabi must measure completion, retest agreement and item fairness for real, and re-tune the thresholds.

status.title: What we see so far
status.offline: We could not reach the results service. Your sessions are saved on this device and will be looked at next time.

body.stable: No meaningful change in what we measure. This is not a full health check. If anything worries you, talk to your doctor any time.
body.watch_context: Your activities were a little different recently. {context} often affects how we feel and focus. We'll do a short check again in a few days.
body.watch: Some of your recent results were different from your usual. This happens for many reasons. We'll do a few short checks over the next days to understand it better.
body.review: Over the last few checks, some results have stayed different from your usual. This is not a diagnosis. It is a good reason to talk with a doctor, who can look at the full picture.
body.urgent: What you described needs urgent medical help. Please call 998 now or go to the nearest emergency department.

status.gap: It has been a while since your last session. A short one today keeps your picture up to date.
status.rangeLabel: Where your recent results sit compared with your usual
status.rangeExplain: The dot shows our best estimate of your recent results. The shaded part shows the range they most likely fall in. A wider shaded part means we are less sure.
status.seePacket: See the summary for your doctor

storyFamily.lower: {task} was a little different from your usual.

routes.emergency: Call 998 or go to the nearest emergency department now.
routes.primary_care_packet: Book a visit with your family doctor and share your summary. They can decide if another specialist should see you.
routes.primary_care_bp_glucose: Your recent blood pressure or sugar readings are above target. Book a visit with your family doctor.
routes.mental_health: You have reported low mood, stress or loneliness for a while. Talking to your family doctor or a mental health service can help.
routes.audiology: A hearing check could help. Ask for an audiology appointment.
routes.optometry: An eye check could help. Ask for an optometry appointment.

onboarding.welcomeBody: We will ask a few questions, check that you can hear and see comfortably, and explain how your information is used. It takes about 3 minutes.
onboarding.aboutBody: This helps us compare you fairly. You can skip anything you prefer not to share.
onboarding.familiarityBody: There are no right answers. This helps us give the right amount of guidance.
familiarityQuestions: Do you use a smartphone every day?
Do you send messages or make video calls on your phone?
Do you feel comfortable trying new apps?
onboarding.hearingPrompt: Press Listen. Can you hear the voice clearly?
onboarding.hearingSample: Hello. This is how Baseline will read instructions to you.
onboarding.noVoice: Your device has no voice for this language. Instructions will be shown as text.
onboarding.visionPrompt: Can you read this sentence easily?
onboarding.assistedPrompt: Will someone usually help you with the activities?
onboarding.consentBody: Choose what Baseline may use. You can change these at any time, and delete all your data.

checkin.title: Quick check-in
checkin.intro: A few questions about today. This helps us understand your results.
checkin.sleepHours: How many hours did you sleep last night?
checkin.loneliness: How lonely have you felt recently?
checkin.ill: Are you unwell or in pain today?
checkin.newMedication: Have you started or changed a medicine this week?
checkin.caffeine: Have you had coffee or tea in the last hour?
checkin.redFlag: Right now, do you have sudden confusion, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or a sudden severe headache?

urgent.title: Please get help now
urgent.body: What you described needs urgent medical help. Please call 998 now or go to the nearest emergency department. If someone is with you, ask them to help.
urgent.back: I made a mistake, go back

shopping.name: Shopping for a family gathering
shopping.intro: You are buying food for a family gathering. Look at the shopping list and try to remember every item. You will see it for 20 seconds.
shopping.recallTitle: Which items were on your list?
shopping.recallBody: Tap every item that was on the list, then press Done.
shopping.delayedIntro: Earlier you saw a shopping list. Let's see which items you still remember.

quick.introChoice: Now a coffee cup or a teapot can appear. Tap the button that matches it as fast as you can.
quick.tooSoon: Too soon. Wait for the cup.

medication.name: Weekly pill organizer
medication.intro: Your doctor gave you new instructions. Put each medicine in the right times of day: morning, noon or night.

health.title: Health profile
health.intro: These questions help us suggest the right healthy steps. They never change what we see in your activities. "Don't know" is always fine.

questions.hearing_loss: Do you have trouble hearing conversations, even with a hearing aid?
questions.vision_loss: Do you have trouble seeing, even with glasses?
questions.hypertension: Has a doctor told you that you have high blood pressure?
questions.diabetes: Has a doctor told you that you have diabetes or high blood sugar?
questions.high_ldl: Has a doctor told you that your cholesterol is high?
questions.obesity: Has a doctor said your weight is affecting your health?
questions.inactivity: On most days, do you walk or move for less than 30 minutes?
questions.smoking: Do you smoke cigarettes, shisha or medwakh?
questions.alcohol: Do you drink more than a few alcoholic drinks a week?
questions.depression: In the last two weeks, have you often felt down or lost interest in things?
questions.social_isolation: Do you often go a week without seeing family or friends?
questions.head_injury: Have you ever had a head injury that knocked you out?
questions.air_pollution: Do you spend a lot of time near heavy traffic, dust or smoke?

health.familyQuestion: Has a parent, brother or sister had serious memory problems in later life?
health.genomicsBody: For this demo only, choose a synthetic APOE result. It is never shown to you as a number. It goes only to your clinician, with an offer of genetic counselling.
health.genomicsOff: Genetic information is turned off. You can turn it on in My data and sharing.
health.whatYouCanDoEmpty: Answer the questions above to see suggestions.

actions.hearing_loss: A hearing check is quick, and hearing aids help many people stay engaged.
actions.vision_loss: An eye check can find problems that are easy to treat, such as cataracts.
actions.hypertension: Keep blood pressure in range: regular readings and follow-up with your doctor.
actions.diabetes: Keep blood sugar in range with your care team: food, activity and medicines.
actions.high_ldl: Ask your doctor about cholesterol checks and treatment.
actions.obesity: Small, steady changes to food and activity help weight and blood pressure.
actions.inactivity: Walking after Maghrib or in a mall counts. Build up to 30 minutes on most days.
actions.smoking: Stopping smoking, shisha or medwakh helps at any age. Your health centre can help.
actions.alcohol: Cutting down on alcohol protects your brain.
actions.depression: Talk to your doctor about low mood. It can be treated, and it matters for memory.
actions.social_isolation: Regular time with family, friends or the majlis keeps the mind active.
actions.head_injury: Protect your head: wear a seat belt, and a helmet when cycling.
actions.air_pollution: On dusty or hazy days, keep windows closed and walk indoors.

health.noScores: We do not calculate a risk number. These are things you can act on.

family.title: Family check-in
family.intro: Someone who knows you well often notices everyday changes first. Ask a family member, friend or caregiver to answer 8 short questions. It takes about 2 minutes.
family.off: Family member input is turned off. You can turn it on in My data and sharing.
family.inviteBody: Share this link, or hand them your phone.
family.privacy: The person you invite sees only these questions, never your results.
family.monthly: Asking once a month works best.
family.formTitle: Questions for a family member or friend
family.formIntro: Think about the last year. Has there been a change in any of these because of thinking or memory problems? Answer only from what you have seen yourself.
family.relationship: How do you know this person?
items: Problems with judgment, for example with money or safety decisions
Less interest in hobbies or activities
Repeating the same questions, stories or statements
Trouble learning to use a new phone, tool or appliance
Forgetting the correct month or year
Trouble handling money matters or bills
Daily problems with thinking or memory
family.thanks: Thank you. Your answers were saved.
family.licence: These questions are AD8-style while permission for the licensed version is pending.

devices.title: Devices and readings
devices.intro: Readings help shape your healthy-steps plan and the summary for your doctor. They do not change what we see in your activities.
devices.off: Health devices are turned off. You can turn them on in My data and sharing.
devices.simBody: For this demo, these buttons stand in for a real Bluetooth cuff, glucometer or watch. Each adds a week of synthetic readings.
devices.simAdded: A week of simulated readings was added.
devices.manualBody: For example: "My pressure was 132 over 84" or "Sugar 110 fasting".
devices.notUnderstood: We could not understand that. Try "132 over 84".
devices.importBody: Load a synthetic Weqaya screening summary. It stands in for importing a real record.
devices.importOff: Health record summaries are turned off. You can turn them on in My data and sharing.
devices.imported: Sample summary loaded. It also added answers to your health profile.
devices.sleepNote: Watch sleep times are estimates. We use only how long and how regular, not sleep stages.

privacy.title: My data and sharing
privacy.intro: Everything stays on this device unless you choose to share it. Turning something off hides it everywhere straight away.
privacy.kept: Turning something off hides it but keeps it on this device, so you can turn it back on. To remove everything, delete all your data.

plan.title: My healthy-steps plan
plan.intro: Small goals that support brain health, based on what you told us and your readings. Pick what suits your week.
plan.evidence: Based on multidomain programmes such as FINGER and US POINTER. These goals help everyone, whatever their genes.

activity.title: Move a little more
activity.body: Walk for 20 minutes on 4 days this week. A mall walk counts.
activity.ramadan: Walk gently for 20 minutes after iftar on 4 days this week.

bp.title: Keep an eye on blood pressure
bp.body: Measure your blood pressure on 3 mornings, resting. If it is 140 over 90 or higher twice, book a visit with your doctor.

glucose.title: Blood sugar follow-up
glucose.body: Check your sugar as your care team advised, and book your next follow-up if it is due.

diet.title: A heart-friendly plate
diet.body: Half the plate vegetables, add fish or beans twice this week, and cut back on salt and sweet drinks.
diet.ramadan: Break the fast with dates and water, keep iftar balanced, and have a slow-energy suhoor such as oats or beans.

sleep.title: A steady sleep routine
sleep.body: Go to bed at the same time on 5 nights, and put screens away 30 minutes before.

hearing.title: Hearing check
hearing.body: Book a hearing check. If you have hearing aids, wear them during conversations.

vision.title: Eye check
vision.body: Book an eye check, and keep your glasses up to date.

social.title: Time with others
social.body: Plan 3 visits or calls with family or friends this week.

mind.title: Keep the mind busy
mind.body: Spend 15 minutes on 3 days learning something new: a recipe, a craft, a language or memorising a passage.

smoking.title: Stopping smoking
smoking.body: Ask your health centre about free support to stop smoking, shisha or medwakh.

mood.title: Looking after your mood
mood.body: Talk to your doctor or someone you trust about how you have been feeling.

packet.title: Summary for my doctor
packet.intro: This is what Baseline would send to your clinic. It is only shared if you choose to share it.

rules.within_range: Recent results within the usual range.
rules.context_explained_drop: A change explained by recorded context, such as sleep or illness.
rules.rc_composite: Overall change beyond the usual range.
rules.rc_two_families: Change in two activity areas at once.
rules.persist_after_retest: The change stayed across independent follow-up checks.
rules.decline_plus_informant: Change in activities, and a family member noticed everyday changes.
rules.rapid_drop: A large change over a short time.
rules.one_stage_gate: Change beyond the review threshold (single-step rule).
rules.hysteresis_hold: Holding the current state until results settle.
rules.recovered: Results returned to the usual range.
rules.review_hold: Waiting for a clinician to review.
rules.red_flag: Sudden symptoms reported; urgent guidance shown.
rules.retest_cleared: Follow-up checks were within the usual range.

packet.trajectoryNote: Line: estimated change from the person's own usual, in personal units. Shaded band: 95% range. Background colour: state at each session.
packet.genomicsPerson: Shared with your clinician only, with an offer of genetic counselling. Not shown here.
packet.counselling: Offer genetic counselling before discussing this result. It does not change prevention advice.
packet.shareBody: Your clinic will see this summary. Nothing else leaves your device.
packet.shareOff: Sharing with your clinic is turned off.

clinic.title: Clinician console
clinic.demoNote: Demo: in a real service this runs at the clinic with sign-in. Here it reads summaries shared on this device.

decisionHelp.accept: Accept: you agree a clinical assessment is warranted and will see the person.
decisionHelp.override: Override: you judge no assessment is needed now. A reason is required and tracked as a quality metric.
decisionHelp.refer_onward: Refer onward: send directly to a specialist service.

clinic.exportLabels: Export outcome labels for the Lab
clinic.labelsNote: Outcomes become labels for checking accuracy against real assessments. Overrides are tracked as a quality metric.
clinic.auditNote: Every message to and from the assistant, with the intent, the tools it used, and whether the reply was template-locked.

chips: What can I do this week?

replies.intro: Hello, I'm {name}, an AI assistant, not a doctor. I can explain what Baseline sees, note a reading like "my pressure was 130 over 80", or help you find a next step.
replies.help: I can tell you what Baseline sees, describe your week, note a blood pressure or sugar reading, suggest this week's healthy step, or open your summary for the doctor. I'm {name}, an AI assistant; for medical questions, please ask your doctor.
replies.identity: I'm {name}, an AI assistant inside Baseline. I'm not a doctor and not a person. Baseline's checks decide what is seen; I only explain them.
replies.diagnosis: Only a doctor can answer that, after a full assessment. I can't tell, and Baseline's checks can't either. If you are worried, share your summary with your clinic so a doctor can look at the full picture.
replies.hide: I can't change, soften or hide what Baseline sees. You do decide who sees it: family members only see their own questions, and nothing goes to your clinic unless you choose to share.
replies.medication: I can't give advice about medicines. Please ask your doctor or pharmacist before starting, stopping or changing any medicine. If you started a new medicine, mention it in your next check-in.
replies.rawNumbers: Baseline doesn't show single numbers, because they move from day to day and can mislead. It looks at your pattern over time. Your summary for the doctor has the details a care team needs.
replies.dependence: I'm glad to help any time, and I'm an AI assistant. The people around you matter most. How about calling a family member or a friend today?
replies.sleepHours: Thanks for telling me you slept {hours} hours. Shall I add that to your next check-in?
replies.sleepPoor: Sorry to hear you slept badly. Sleep can change how the activities feel. Shall I note it for your next check-in?
replies.sleepSaved: Noted. It will be filled in on your next check-in, and you can change it there.
replies.readingConfirm: I heard {type}: {value}. Shall I save it?
replies.readingSavedHigh: Saved. This reading is above the usual target. One reading is not a pattern; if it stays high, book a visit with your doctor.
replies.deviceOff: Health devices are turned off, so I didn't save it. You can turn them on in My data and sharing.
replies.noResults: I can't see your results right now. Your sessions are saved on this device.
replies.building: Your baseline is still being set: {done} of {total} sessions done. Each short session helps.
replies.planEmpty: Your healthy-steps plan is ready to look at.
replies.packet: Here is your summary for the doctor. You choose whether to share it.
replies.family: Someone close to you can answer 8 short questions about everyday changes. You control what they see.
replies.retest: A short follow-up check would help. I've set a reminder for {date}.
replies.scheduleReview: The next step is a talk with your doctor. Your summary is ready to share.
replies.scheduleNormal: Keep to your usual routine: a short session on most days is plenty.
replies.greeting: Hello! I'm {name}. How can I help today?
replies.unknown: I'm not sure I understood. I can tell you what Baseline sees, describe your week, note a reading, or open your summary for the doctor.

design.title: Design system
design.intro: Building blocks for Baseline: large text, large touch targets, calm colors, and right-to-left support.

stateHints.stable: No meaningful change in what we measure.
stateHints.watch: Something changed. We will check again soon.
stateHints.review: Worth discussing with a doctor. Not a diagnosis.
